newsitem.title: MEXICO: Mexico Northeast railway sees mid-June operations.
newsitem.headline: Mexico Northeast railway sees mid-June operations.

text.p: Mexico's Northeast Railway should begin to be operated by its new private owners by mid-June, Transportacion Maritima Mexicana (TMM) spokesman Fernando Ruiz Huarte said.
"I believe that at about the middle of June we should begin operations," Ruiz said in a phone interview late Monday.

TMM and Kansas City Southern Industries recently won a privatisation auction for the Northeast Railway with a $1.4 billion bid. They set up Transportacion Ferroviaria Mexicana (TFM) to run the venture.
TMM and Kansas City Southern originally aimed for a May 15 start-up date for the railway, but backed off the earlier plans amid labor difficulties, officials said..
The companies are required to make the final payment of about $840 million on the rail by July, but officials say they hope to make an early payment to speed up initial operations.
Financing problems led the government to take an up to 33.5 percent "temporary" stake in the venture, which it will claim in this final payment.

TFM is planning a $250 million zero-coupon bond offer and $150 million in a 10-yr Yankee bond to replace a more expensive bridge loan. The funds will be used to pay the government what the company owes on the Northeast Railroad.
